newsitem.title: USA: Immunex says drug safe in six month study.
newsitem.headline: Immunex says drug safe in six month study.

text.p: Immunex Corp said Friday that preliminary results from an ongoing safety trial for its drug ENBREL suggest the drug can be safely administered to patients with rheumatoid arthritis for at least six months.

According to early results of an open-label study reported at a meeting in Chicago, 41 patients received the drug for at least six months, and none of the patients had to withdraw because of injection site reactions or infections.

Dr. Larry Moreland of the University of Alabama at Birmingham said in the study that injection site reactions were relatively mild and infrequent, with 146 site reactions out of a total 3,708 injections.
Infections, including colds, affected 16 of 41 patients during 260 patient months of treatment, and all infections resolved. No antibodies against the drug were detected.
Immunex also said improvements in clinical endpoints were consistent with previously reported results.
The ongoing, open-label, multi-center study is designed to measure the long-term safety of Enbrel on 105 patients who will receive the drug for at least a year.

Concurrently, Immunex is doing a Phase III double-blind study to prove the drug's effectiveness on severe arthritis. If successful the company hopes to file an application for U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval next year, a spokeswoman said.
ENBREL is a soluble tumor necrosis factor receptor and part of a new class of biologic drugs aimed at inhibiting the biological effects of tumor necrosis factor.
